claim: USB-to-NVMe bridge chip families and their UASP/TRIM/SMART support on Linux, verification commands, and the hidden-TRIM quirk.

claim: On UEFI only one ESP is active, so installers write EFI files to the internal ESP even when the bootloader target is the USB drive; clearing the esp flag during install avoids it.
quote: The major problem with installing Linux on an external USB drive on UEFI systems is that a system can only have one active ESP (EFI System Partition) at a time.
